types.name: Retainable
types.doc:
Attached object for types that can have delayed destruction.
Retainable works as an attached property that allows objects to be
kept around (retained) after they would normally be destroyed, which
is especially useful for things like exit transitions.

An object that is retainable will have @@Retainable as an attached property.
All retainable objects will say that they are retainable on their respective
typeinfo pages.

> [!INFO] Working directly with @@Retainable is often overly complicated and
> error prone. For this reason @@RetainableLock should
> usually be used instead.

properties.name: retained
properties.doc: If the object is currently in a retained state.

functions.name: lock
functions.doc:
Hold a lock on the object so it cannot be destroyed.

A counter is used to ensure you can lock the object from multiple places
and it will not be unlocked until the same number of unlocks as locks have occurred.

> [!WARNING] It is easy to forget to unlock a locked object.
> Doing so will create what is effectively a memory leak.
>
> Using @@RetainableLock is recommended as it will help
> avoid this scenario and make misuse more obvious.

functions.name: unlock
functions.doc: Remove a lock on the object. See @@lock() for more information.

functions.name: forceUnlock
functions.doc:
Forcibly remove all locks, destroying the object.

@@unlock() should usually be preferred.

signals.name: dropped
signals.doc:
This signal is sent when the object would normally be destroyed.

If all signal handlers return and no locks are in place, the object will be destroyed.
If at least one lock is present the object will be retained until all are removed.

signals.name: aboutToDestroy
signals.doc:
This signal is sent immediately before the object is destroyed.
At this point destruction cannot be interrupted.

types.uncreatable_reason: Retainable can only be used as an attached object.

types.name: RetainableLock
types.doc:
A helper for easily using Retainable.
A RetainableLock provides extra safety and ease of use for locking
@@Retainable objects. A retainable object can be locked by multiple
locks at once, and each lock re-exposes relevant properties
of the retained objects.

#### Example
The code below will keep a retainable object alive for as long as the
RetainableLock exists.

```qml
RetainableLock {
  object: aRetainableObject
  locked: true
}
```

properties.name: object
properties.doc: The object to lock. Must be @@Retainable.

properties.name: locked
properties.doc: If the object should be locked.

properties.name: retained
properties.doc: If the object is currently in a retained state.

signals.name: dropped
signals.doc: Rebroadcast of the object's @@Retainable.dropped(s).

signals.name: aboutToDestroy
signals.doc: Rebroadcast of the object's @@Retainable.aboutToDestroy(s).

types.name: PopupAdjustment
types.doc:
Adjustment strategy for popups that do not fit on screen.
Adjustment strategy for popups. See @@PopupAnchor.adjustment.

Adjustment flags can be combined with the `|` operator.

`Flip` will be applied first, then `Slide`, then `Resize`.

values.name: SlideX
values.doc: If the X axis is constrained, the popup will slide along the X axis until it fits onscreen.

values.name: SlideY
values.doc: If the Y axis is constrained, the popup will slide along the Y axis until it fits onscreen.

values.name: Slide
values.doc: Alias for `SlideX | SlideY`.

values.name: FlipX
values.doc: If the X axis is constrained, the popup will invert its horizontal gravity if any.

values.name: FlipY
values.doc: If the Y axis is constrained, the popup will invert its vertical gravity if any.

values.name: Flip
values.doc: Alias for `FlipX | FlipY`.

values.name: ResizeX
values.doc: If the X axis is constrained, the width of the popup will be reduced to fit on screen.

values.name: ResizeY
values.doc: If the Y axis is constrained, the height of the popup will be reduced to fit on screen.

values.name: Resize
values.doc: Alias for `ResizeX | ResizeY`

values.name: All
values.doc: Alias for `Flip | Slide | Resize`.

types.name: PopupAnchor
types.doc: Anchorpoint or positioner for popup windows.

properties.name: window
properties.doc: The window to anchor / attach the popup to. Setting this property unsets @@item.

properties.name: item
properties.doc:
The item to anchor / attach the popup to. Setting this property unsets @@window.

The popup's position relative to its parent window is only calculated when it is
initially shown (directly before @@anchoring(s) is emitted), meaning its anchor
rectangle will be set relative to the item's position in the window at that time.
@@updateAnchor() can be called to update the anchor rectangle if the item's position
has changed.

> [!NOTE] If a more flexible way to position a popup relative to an item is needed,
> set @@window to the item's parent window, and handle the @@anchoring signal to
> position the popup relative to the window's contentItem.

properties.name: rect
properties.doc:
The anchorpoints the popup will attach to, relative to @@item or @@window.
Which anchors will be used is determined by the @@edges, @@gravity, and @@adjustment.

If using @@item, the default anchor rectangle matches the dimensions of the item.

If you leave @@edges, @@gravity and @@adjustment at their default values,
setting more than `x` and `y` does not matter. The anchor rect cannot
be smaller than 1x1 pixels.

[coordinate mapping functions]: https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qml-qtquick-item.html#mapFromItem-method

properties.name: margins
properties.doc:
A margin applied to the anchor rect.

This is most useful when @@item is used and @@rect is left at its default
value (matching the Item's dimensions).

properties.name: edges
properties.doc:
The point on the anchor rectangle the popup should anchor to.
Opposing edges suchs as `Edges.Left | Edges.Right` are not allowed.

Defaults to `Edges.Top | Edges.Left`.

properties.name: gravity
properties.doc:
The direction the popup should expand towards, relative to the anchorpoint.
Opposing edges suchs as `Edges.Left | Edges.Right` are not allowed.

Defaults to `Edges.Bottom | Edges.Right`.

properties.name: adjustment
properties.doc:
The strategy used to adjust the popup's position if it would otherwise not fit on screen,
based on the anchor @@rect, preferred @@edges, and @@gravity.

types.name: SystemClock
types.doc:
System clock accessor.
SystemClock is a view into the system's clock.
It updates at hour, minute, or second intervals depending on @@precision.

# Examples
```qml
SystemClock {
  id: clock
  precision: SystemClock.Seconds
}

@@QtQuick.Text {
  text: Qt.formatDateTime(clock.date, "hh:mm:ss - yyyy-MM-dd")
}
```

> [!WARNING] Clock updates will trigger within 50ms of the system clock changing,
> however this can be either before or after the clock changes (+-50ms). If you
> need a date object, use @@date instead of constructing a new one, or the time
> of the constructed object could be off by up to a second.

properties.name: enabled
properties.doc:
If the clock should update. Defaults to true.

Setting enabled to false pauses the clock.

properties.name: precision
properties.doc: The precision the clock should measure at. Defaults to `SystemClock.Seconds`.

properties.name: date
properties.doc:
The current date and time.

> [!TIP] You can use @@QtQml.Qt.formatDateTime() to get the time as a string in
> your format of choice.

properties.name: hours
properties.doc: The current hour.

properties.name: minutes
properties.doc: The current minute, or 0 if @@precision is `SystemClock.Hours`.

properties.name: seconds
properties.doc: The current second, or 0 if @@precision is `SystemClock.Hours` or `SystemClock.Minutes`.

types.name: ScriptModel
types.doc:
QML model reflecting a javascript expression
ScriptModel is a QML [Data Model] that generates model operations based on changes
to a javascript expression attached to @@values.

### When should I use this
ScriptModel should be used when you would otherwise use a javascript expression as a model,
[QAbstractItemModel] is accepted, and the data is likely to change over the lifetime of the program.

When directly using a javascript expression as a model, types like @@QtQuick.Repeater or @@QtQuick.ListView
will destroy all created delegates, and re-create the entire list. In the case of @@QtQuick.ListView this
will also prevent animations from working. If you wrap your expression with ScriptModel, only new items
will be created, and ListView animations will work as expected.

### Example
```qml
// Will cause all delegates to be re-created every time filterText changes.
@@QtQuick.Repeater {
  model: myList.filter(entry => entry.name.startsWith(filterText))
  delegate: // ...
}

// Will add and remove delegates only when required.
@@QtQuick.Repeater {
  model: ScriptModel {
    values: myList.filter(entry => entry.name.startsWith(filterText))
  }

  delegate: // ...
}
```
[QAbstractItemModel]: https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qabstractitemmodel.html
[Data Model]: https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtquick-modelviewsdata-modelview.html#qml-data-models

properties.name: values
properties.doc:
The list of values to reflect in the model.
> [!WARNING] ScriptModel currently only works with lists of *unique* values.
> There must not be any duplicates in the given list, or behavior of the model is undefined.

> [!TIP] @@ObjectModel$s supplied by Quickshell types will only contain unique values,
> and can be used like so:
>
> ```qml
> ScriptModel {
>   values: DesktopEntries.applications.values.filter(...)
> }
> ```
>
> Note that we are using @@ObjectModel.values because it will cause @@ScriptModel.values
> to receive an update on change.

> [!TIP] Most lists exposed by Quickshell are read-only. Some operations like `sort()`
> act on a list in-place and cannot be used directly on a list exposed by Quickshell.
> You can copy a list using spread syntax: `[...variable]` instead of `variable`.
>
> For example:
> ```qml
> ScriptModel {
>   values: [...DesktopEntries.applications.values].sort(...)
> }
> ```

properties.name: objectProp
properties.doc:
The property that javascript objects passed into the model will be compared with.

For example, if `objectProp` is `"myprop"` then `{ myprop: "a", other: "y" }` and
`{ myprop: "a", other: "z" }` will be considered equal.

Defaults to `""`, meaning no key.

properties.name: comparisonMode
properties.doc:
How values should be compared. Defaults to `ObjectComparison.Structure`.

Identity based comparison is faster if usable for a given model, and often
achievable with @@objectProp.

types.name: ColorQuantizer
types.doc:
Color Quantization Utility
A color quantization utility used for getting prevalent colors in an image, by
averaging out the image's color data recursively.

#### Example
```qml
ColorQuantizer {
  id: colorQuantizer
  source: Qt.resolvedUrl("./yourImage.png")
  depth: 3 // Will produce 8 colors (2³)
  rescaleSize: 64 // Rescale to 64x64 for faster processing
}
```

properties.name: colors
properties.doc:
Access the colors resulting from the color quantization performed.
> [!NOTE] The amount of colors returned from the quantization is determined by
> the property depth, specifically 2ⁿ where n is the depth.

properties.name: source
properties.doc: Path to the image you'd like to run the color quantization on.

properties.name: depth
properties.doc:
Max depth for the color quantization. Each level of depth represents another
binary split of the color space

properties.name: imageRect
properties.doc:
Rectangle that the source image is cropped to.

Can be set to `undefined` to reset.

properties.name: rescaleSize
properties.doc:
The size to rescale the image to, when rescaleSize is 0 then no scaling will be done.
> [!NOTE] Results from color quantization doesn't suffer much when rescaling, it's
> recommended to rescale, otherwise the quantization process will take much longer.

types.name: Bluetooth

Bluetooth manager
Provides access to bluetooth devices and adapters.

properties.name: defaultAdapter
properties.doc: The default bluetooth adapter. Usually there is only one.

properties.name: adapters
properties.doc: A list of all bluetooth adapters. See @@defaultAdapter for the default.

A list of all connected bluetooth devices across all adapters.
See @@BluetoothAdapter.devices for the devices connected to a single adapter.

values.name: Enabled

types.name: BluetoothAdapter
types.doc: A Bluetooth adapter

properties.name: name
properties.doc: System provided name of the adapter. See @@adapterId for the internal identifier.

properties.name: enabled
properties.doc: True if the adapter is currently enabled. More detailed state is available from @@state.

properties.name: state
properties.doc: Detailed power state of the adapter.

properties.name: discoverable
properties.doc: True if the adapter can be discovered by other bluetooth devices.

properties.name: discoverableTimeout
properties.doc:
Timeout in seconds for how long the adapter stays discoverable after @@discoverable is set to true.
A value of 0 means the adapter stays discoverable forever.

properties.name: discovering
properties.doc: True if the adapter is scanning for new devices.

properties.name: pairable
properties.doc:
True if the adapter is accepting incoming pairing requests.

This only affects incoming pairing requests and should typically only be changed
by system settings applications. Defaults to true.

properties.name: pairableTimeout
properties.doc:
Timeout in seconds for how long the adapter stays pairable after @@pairable is set to true.
A value of 0 means the adapter stays pairable forever. Defaults to 0.

properties.name: devices
properties.doc: Bluetooth devices connected to this adapter.

properties.name: adapterId

values.name: Disconnected
values.doc: The device is not connected.

values.name: Connected
values.doc: The device is connected.

values.name: Disconnecting
values.doc: The device is disconnecting.

values.name: Connecting

types.name: BluetoothDevice
types.doc: A tracked Bluetooth device.

properties.name: address
properties.doc: MAC address of the device.

properties.name: name
properties.doc:
The name of the Bluetooth device. This property may be written to create an alias, or set to
an empty string to fall back to the device provided name.

See @@deviceName for the name provided by the device.

properties.name: deviceName
properties.doc:
The name of the Bluetooth device, ignoring user provided aliases. See also @@name
which returns a user provided alias if set.

properties.name: icon
properties.doc: System icon representing the device type. Use @@Quickshell.Quickshell.iconPath() to display this in an image.

properties.name: state
properties.doc: Connection state of the device.

properties.name: connected
properties.doc:
True if the device is currently connected to the computer.

Setting this property is equivalent to calling @@connect() and @@disconnect().

> [!NOTE] @@state provides more detailed information if required.

properties.name: paired
properties.doc:
True if the device is paired to the computer.

> [!NOTE] @@pair() can be used to pair a device, however you must @@forget() the device to unpair it.

properties.name: bonded
properties.doc: True if pairing information is stored for future connections.

properties.name: pairing
properties.doc:
True if the device is currently being paired.

> [!NOTE] @@cancelPair() can be used to cancel the pairing process.

properties.name: trusted
properties.doc:
True if the device is considered to be trusted by the system.
Trusted devices are allowed to reconnect themselves to the system without intervention.

properties.name: blocked
properties.doc:
True if the device is blocked from connecting.
If a device is blocked, any connection attempts will be immediately rejected by the system.

properties.name: wakeAllowed
properties.doc: True if the device is allowed to wake up the host system from suspend.

properties.name: batteryAvailable
properties.doc: True if the connected device reports its battery level. Battery level can be accessed via @@battery.

properties.name: battery
properties.doc: Battery level of the connected device, from `0.0` to `1.0`. Only valid if @@batteryAvailable is true.

properties.name: adapter
properties.doc: The Bluetooth adapter this device belongs to.

properties.name: dbusPath
properties.doc: DBus path of the device under the `org.bluez` system service.

functions.name: connect
functions.doc: Attempt to connect to the device.

functions.name: disconnect
functions.doc: Disconnect from the device.

functions.name: pair
functions.doc:
Attempt to pair the device.

> [!NOTE] @@paired and @@pairing return the current pairing status of the device.

functions.name: cancelPair
functions.doc: Cancel an active pairing attempt.

functions.name: forget
functions.doc: Forget the device.
